text.p: New excerpts from recently declassified U.S. Army training manuals for the South American military teach the use of executions, press censorship and Molotov cocktails, according to materials released Wednesday by Representative Joseph Kennedy.

One of the now-obsolete government manuals branded Tom Hayden -- a founding member of the Students for a Democratic Society in the 1960s and now a California state senator -- as "one of the masters of terrorist planning."
In a statement, Hayden called the assertion "psychotic fabrications at taxpayer expense."
Kennedy, a Massachusetts Democrat, said the manuals, used at the Army School of the Americas and distributed in South America years ago, is one more reason why the school should be abolished.
He said the manuals "provide direct evidence that the school has not only failed to serve its mission but has subverted its mission. It's time to close down the School of the Americas."
The school at the Army's Fort Benning, Georgia, trains military officers, police and civilians from Latin America.
Representative Sam Farr, a California Demcorat, said the school "has tarnished military education in America."
The Defence Department released some excerpts from the manuals Friday. Kennedy obtained copies and released other excerpts, while his staff continued translating the rest from Spanish.
The Army said practices suggested in the manuals had been U.S. policy as late as the 1960s but were outlawed in the 1980s. Among the new portions released by Kennedy:

-- "A deserter (from a guerrilla group) could be more or less certain that there will be no reprisals against him if all other members of his cell are eliminated by security forces. ... This circumstance could be used to persuade insurgent deserters to provide information to the government."
-- Later, it suggests using "arrests, execution or pacification" to eliminate guerrilla organisations which have been infiltrated by the government.
-- Censorship is recommended, primarily for "war correspondents, radio commentators and press photographers" and also for material prepared in areas under the jurisdiction of the armed forces.
-- One manual suggests employing women in some circumstances. It cautions they are "more emotional than men," but adds there is "no difference in their intelligence."
-- One manual contains detailed instructions for making the firebombs known as Molotov cocktails, calling them "one of the most effective fire artifacts developed during World War II."
